title: Evidence for Distributed Fault Energetics and Their Impact on Deformation in a Chemically Complex Alloy
authors: Kaijun Yin, Jun-Ping Du, Peijun Yu, Rui Feng, Hanyu Hou, Haw-Wen Hsiao, Ke An, Peter K. Liaw, Shigenobu Ogata, Jian-Min Zuo
abstract: Chemically complex alloys feature intrinsically heterogeneous local chemical environments and, consequently, fluctuations in local fault energetics. However, experimentally quantifying their relationship remains challenging, leaving the role of this distributed energy landscape in deformation mechanisms incompletely resolved. Here, we develop a distribution based framework linking experimentally measured stacking fault widths to deformation relevant apparent fault energy, revealing a distributed local fault-energy landscape in CrCoNi. The framework reveals the stabilizing role of energy fluctuations and captures an upward shift in the apparent fault energetics, from negative values toward zero following heat treatment, which atomistic simulations associate with the emergence of L12 type chemical short-range order. Using one-dimensional kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, supported by electron microscopy observations, we further show that history-dependent changes in the local fault-energy landscape bias the competition among stacking faulting, nano-twinning and HCP transformation in CrCoNi. Our results provide an experimentally anchored, distribution-based framework for understanding deformation in chemically complex alloys as it evolves within a distributed fault-energy landscape shaped by local chemical order.
summary: This work establishes a distribution-based framework to understand how local chemical disorder dictates mechanical deformation in complex alloys like CrCoNi. By linking measured fault widths to the apparent fault energy landscape, the authors show that energy fluctuations are stabilizing and that thermal history dictates the competition between various deformation mechanisms. This provides a crucial, experimentally grounded tool for materials science.
main_problem: Quantifying the role of the distributed local fault energy landscape in the deformation mechanisms of chemically complex alloys is experimentally challenging.
main_result: The study reveals a distributed local fault-energy landscape in CrCoNi, showing that energy fluctuations stabilize the system and that heat treatment causes an upward shift in apparent fault energetics, which biases deformation pathways.
method: The authors develop a distribution-based framework linking measured stacking fault widths to apparent fault energy, supported by kinetic Monte Carlo simulations and electron microscopy observations.
model_or_system: The system studied is a chemically complex alloy, specifically CrCoNi. The model involves analyzing the local fault-energy landscape, which is influenced by local chemical order (e.g., L12 type short-range order).
key_observables: Experimentally measured stacking fault widths, apparent fault energy, and the competition between stacking faulting, nano-twinning, and HCP transformation.
important_parameters: Local chemical environment heterogeneity, temperature/heat treatment history, and the resulting local fault energy distribution.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the local fault energy landscape can be described by a distribution derived from experimental measurements.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of quantifying distributed fault energetics in complex alloys, develops a distribution-based framework using experimental data (stacking fault widths), and then applies this framework using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations and microscopy to show history-dependent biasing of deformation modes.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the use of kinetic Monte Carlo simulations and developing a distribution-based framework to model complex, history-dependent energy landscapes shares methodological overlap with modeling non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems or disordered quantum materials.
